text:
William Nylander is in the middle of the Maple Leafs' most miserable stretch of the season. Toronto has lost almost every game since Halloween, practice was cancelled during the slide, and the headlines have moved to his no-trade clause. After Saturday's loss to Columbus, he called his giveaway on the tying goal a "dumb play", in Daily Faceoff Toronto's words.

His own numbers split two ways. He has 11 goals and 25 points in 25 games, shooting 18%, close to his usual rate, though still a little ahead of the chances. But only six points have come in his last ten games, and the Leafs are drowning at five on five with him: 43% of the expected goals, 5.6 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey flagged that cost last season too, with opponents getting more chances when he played.

The talent is unchanged. His 99.3 mph top shot ranks at the very top of the league, and he still sets up teammates at a top-10% rate. We project about 89 points, but in Toronto right now, the conversation is not about points.
headline: Nylander is scoring, and Toronto is sinking
